title: ISSUE_04_AGENTCORE_SECURITY_FIREBREAK
universal_lens: The security firebreak establishes a measure-theoretic boundary condition on the agent's action space. By imposing a default-deny prior, the system restricts the support of the control distribution to an explicitly defined allowlist, ensuring that unauthorized high-impact operations have strictly zero probability under nominal conditions.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, this maps to a conformal inference filter over tactical event streams. The default-deny policy acts as a strict non-conformity score threshold; any inferred play or data mutation falling outside the calibrated permission matrix is rejected, maintaining epistemic integrity against adversarial noise injection.
gse_mapping: For GSE situational reasoning, the firebreak defines a hard constraint on the state-transition graph. Valid transitions are restricted to those explicitly authorized by the tool permission matrix, preventing the simulation engine from entering undefined or catastrophic states via unbounded resource allocation.

primitives.name: Default-Deny Measure Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: # Issue 04: AgentCore security firebreak ## Context Future agents need default-deny permissions.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: A: Action space (dimensionless set); P(a): Probability measure over actions; \mathcal{W}: Explicit allowlist subset of A.
primitives.assumptions: The total action space A is well-defined and countable. The allowlist \mathcal{W} is a proper subset of A.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breakdown occurs if \mathcal{W} approaches A (loss of restriction) or if the evaluation metric for inclusion in \mathcal{W} becomes collinear with adversarial objectives.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to setting the baseline intensity of a Poisson point process governing agent actions to zero everywhere except on the explicitly whitelisted domains.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of blocked action attempts outside \mathcal{W}.

primitives.name: High-Impact Authority Nullifier
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Why It Matters Agents must not gain deploy, paid-resource, publishing, or source-automation authority by default.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \mathcal{H}: Set of high-impact authorities (deploy, paid-resource, etc.); \delta_{\mathcal{H}}(a): Indicator function for high-impact actions.
primitives.assumptions: High-impact authorities can be perfectly categorized into a disjoint set \mathcal{H}. System resources are bounded.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity arises if semantic drift allows standard actions to implicitly trigger elements of \mathcal{H}, bypassing the nullifier.

layer2.mapping: Maps to a projection operator in GSE that zeroes out velocity vectors pointing toward costly or irreversible simulation states unless explicitly overridden by a human oracle.
layer2.telemetry: Zero-cost execution verification for all non-whitelisted API calls.

primitives.name: Failure Mode Reversibility Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: listed. - Tool permissions are explicit. - Failure modes and rollback paths exist. ## Files Likely
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: S_t: System state at time t; R: Rollback operator mapping S_{t+\Delta} \rightarrow S_t; \epsilon: Residual state divergence.
primitives.assumptions: The system state space admits a continuous or discrete inverse mapping for all permitted transitions. State snapshots are persistently stored.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Irreversible entropy generation where \epsilon > \text{tolerance}, making exact rollback mathematically impossible (e.g., external side-effects).

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to enforcing time-reversibility constraints in GSE Markov chains, ensuring every forward transition has a validated backward edge to prevent absorbing failure states.
layer2.telemetry: Successful restoration rate of S_t after triggered failure modes.

The mathematical foundation of the AgentCore security firebreak rests on defining a constrained optimization landscape where the objective function (agent utility) is heavily penalized outside a predefined safe manifold. We begin by formalizing the 'default-deny' requirement as a Dirac delta prior over the action space, concentrating all probability mass exclusively on the `AGENT_TOOL_PERMISSION_MATRIX`. This creates a sparse control distribution. The 'authority nullification' primitive acts as a hard barrier function, assigning infinite cost to any trajectory attempting to access deploy or paid-resource nodes without explicit cryptographic authorization. 

From a dynamical systems perspective, the agent operates within a phase space where certain regions—representing source-automation or publishing—are designated as forbidden zones. The firebreak ensures the vector field guiding the agent never points toward these zones. Furthermore, the inclusion of 'failure modes and rollback paths' introduces a topological requirement: the allowed state space must be contractible, or at least possess well-defined retractions. If the agent enters an anomalous state due to environmental noise, the rollback operator provides a continuous path back to a known safe equilibrium. 

The duality here lies between exploration and safety. Standard reinforcement learning encourages broad exploration, but the firebreak imposes a strict geometric boundary. The risk identified in the source—that future implementations could exceed documented permissions—represents a gradient leakage where the learned policy slowly expands its support beyond the allowlist. To counter this, we require a continuous verification metric, akin to a Lyapunov function, that monotonically decreases whenever the agent's state approaches the boundary of the permission matrix. The test plan, involving `npm run fable:evidence`, serves as the empirical validation of this Lyapunov stability, ensuring the theoretical bounds hold under stochastic real-world inputs.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This framework inherits directly from Bell-LaPadula mandatory access controls and the principle of least privilege in classical cybersecurity. Mathematically, it echoes the development of constrained Hamiltonian systems in physics, where gauge symmetries restrict physical trajectories. In modern AI alignment, it parallels the 'scoped agency' models proposed to prevent instrumental convergence, ensuring agents do not acquire terminal goals like self-preservation or resource acquisition by default.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: We model the opposing actor as an adversarial optimizer seeking to maximize the agent's effective action radius. This adversary might attempt prompt injection or environment manipulation to trick the agent into perceiving a high-impact action as a benign, whitelisted operation. The decision actor (the security architect) anticipates this by decoupling the semantic interpretation of a request from its execution privileges. The firebreak assumes the agent is inherently myopic regarding long-term consequences, necessitating an external, immutable constraint layer that cannot be reasoned away by the agent's internal logic.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Anti-collinearity is enforced by ensuring the reward signal driving the agent's primary task is orthogonal to the permission escalation vector. If an agent discovers that triggering a 'deploy' action yields a massive shortcut to its goal, the veto mechanism must activate. Leakage occurs if the tool permission matrix contains ambiguous entries that map multiple distinct underlying APIs to a single benign token. The cross-layer veto requires a strict one-to-one mapping between abstract tools and concrete system calls, verified continuously during the `fable:evidence` runtime to prevent semantic aliasing attacks.
